name: AI incidents & governance
summary: US seized infrastructure of a North Korean scheme using deepfake video calls, tied by the FBI to $400m in crypto theft
state: The US Justice Department seized cloud infrastructure behind a North Korean scheme that used fake video meetings, including AI-generated deepfakes of cryptocurrency figures, to trick targets into installing malware; the FBI ties it to more than $400m stolen over 18 months (ID Tech, 13 Nov). On 6 Nov US prosecutors charged three men over a $129m fraud using AI to impersonate chief executives (ID Tech). Searches on 18 Nov found no AI-enabled attack on critical infrastructure and no AI-attributed mass harm, so significant misuse keeps Watch.
for_you: Deepfake voice and video fraud mostly targets businesses and crypto users. The UK National Cyber Security Centre and Action Fraud publish guidance on verifying unexpected payment or software requests.
rubric_hit: Watch: significant AI misuse incident (deepfake video-call scheme tied to $400m theft, disrupted 13 Nov); no AI attack on critical infrastructure

sources.title: ID Tech — US disrupts North Korean fake video call scheme tied to $400 million theft
ID Tech — US charges three in $129 million fraud using AI to pose as CEOs

why: Powerful AI systems are being deployed faster than safeguards; serious incidents or governance breakdowns carry systemic risk.
drivers: Model releases, misuse incidents, regulation, compute controls, deepfakes in elections.

rubric.alert: AI-enabled attack on critical infrastructure, or AI-attributed mass harm event.
rubric.watch: A significant AI misuse incident, major deepfake disruption, or regulatory confrontation.
rubric.normal: No serious AI-attributed harm events or governance shocks this week.
